text:
julie-cs: Customer reported duplicate tokens billed after SSE reconnects. They see partial last chunk repeated and charged twice. Repro attached (curl).

devon-runtime: Can you paste the curl and the chunk boundaries? sounds like last-event-id logic might be off.

julie-cs: Repro snippet they used:
```bash
curl -v -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-latest'
```
They say connection drops after ~28s and client reconnects, then receives the last partial line again (same tokens) and billing shows duplicate tokens.

sam-sre: Do we have ALB/nginx in front of them? ALB idle timeout is 30s by default which could kill connections. If client reconnects and server resends last in-flight chunk we could double-bill.

erin-support: Customer is behind a corporate proxy (Envoy) and our logs show a 502 at upstream at 2198765460, then reconnect at 2198765462.

michael-eng: What are we sending for keepalive? We currently send comment pings as `:heartbeat

` every 60s server-side only when no data. TCP keepalive on the OS is separate (default 2h on linux). That mismatch is dangerous for intermediate proxies.

devon-runtime: Interesting — they drop at ~28s not 60s. That suggests an idle window from the proxy or client (30s-ish). Suggest reduce comment ping to 15s for streaming endpoints, and include an application-level seq/id per chunk so client can dedupe on resume.

sam-sre: Also check ALB/ELB idle timeout and any proxies: if idle window < comment ping interval you'll see drops. Action item: audit common reverse proxies in private nets and our edge config.

erin-support: Customer logs show they include `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect with value `evt-1732`. Our access logs show we returned `id: evt-1732` on the last full event, but the partial tokens were not framed with an id (we only assign ids on full-choice frames). So client can't signal the exact offset.

michael-eng: That explains duplication. On reconnect, client asks to resume from the last event id we provided, but if the last thing they had was a partial chunk with no id, server resends from the previous id (which does not include the partial suffix), and the client receives the partial continuation again. Two problems: (1) we bill when tokens are emitted, (2) we lack re-attach metadata for partial frames.

devon-runtime: Proposed fixes (short term and medium):
- short term: send comment ping every 15s, change default SSE comment format to `:keepalive <monotonic-ts>

` so proxies see activity.
- medium: attach `id:` to every chunk boundary (even partial) and add `stream-offset` header in the event payload so resume is exact.
- billing mitigation: don't finalize billing for an in-flight partial chunk until commit/ack or N seconds after last write; track tokens by (request-id, chunk-offset) to dedupe billing on resume.

sam-sre: For immediate customer relief we can flip the keepalive from 60s->15s on the streaming-prod route and add a canary. Also reach out to infra to check ELB/ALB idle timers in the affected region.

erin-support: Customer agreed to test a canary we deploy. They can also set their client to send `Last-Event-ID` less aggressively (or de-dup client-side) but better to fix server-side.

julie-cs: Repro logs attached in case notes: shows chunk boundary and timestamps. Customer requests timeline for a fix — they saw $0.40 extra billing per reconnect which is significant for bursty integration.

michael-eng: I'll add a runtime ticket: RT-2345 with patch to include `id` on every chunk and stream-offset metadata, and a follow-up RT to change billing to be idempotent by (request-id, offset). Will also push keepalive TTL change to 15s behind a feature flag.

devon-runtime: Implementation note: make sure we don't bloat the stream with huge ids; use a compact monotonic sequence (e.g., `s-173243`) and include a short CRC of the frame so the client can verify. Also include an HTTP header `X-Stream-Liveness: ts=<unix>,seq=<n>` on initial handshake so proxies can see activity at connection start.

sam-sre: Ops checklist for rollout:
- flip keepalive flag on canary pool (us-east-1 small subset)
- monitor dropped connections, reconnection rate, and duplicate-token billing metric
- verify ALB metrics for downstream 502/504s in the same windows

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-089, assigned to michael-eng and sam-sre.

erin-support: I'll loop in the customer with canary details and ask them to validate within their proxy window.

michael-eng: Thanks — will link PR and RT here once ready. If we need rollback, revert keepalive flag and revert id-on-chunk change.

devon-runtime: Long-term, consider a streaming protocol repeatable resume token (binary offset) and a billing contract that bills only on confirmed commit events. For now the chunk-id + shorter comment ping + billing dedupe should fix the customer pain. :thumbsup:

julie-cs: Customer verified reduced reconnects when proxy idle threshold increased and will test canary. Closing loop when they confirm.
